pob.text: There was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim[a], from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

pob.text: That man used to go up from his city year after year to worship and to sacrifice to Yahweh of Armies at Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli[a], Hophni and Phinehas, were there as priests of Yahweh.

pob.text: And her rival would provoke her bitterly in order to irritate her[a], because Yahweh had closed her womb.

spob.text: The other wife, who was Hannah’s rival, would cruelly taunt her to make her miserable, because Yahweh had closed Hannah’s womb and kept her from having children.

pob.text: And so it happened year after year: whenever she went up to the house of Yahweh[a], Peninnah would provoke her[b], and she would weep and not eat.

pob.text: Then Elkanah her husband said to her[a], “Hannah, why are you weeping? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart troubled? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

pob.text: After they had eaten in Shiloh[a], and after they had drunk, Hannah rose. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the temple of Yahweh.

pob.text: She made a vow and said[a], “O Yahweh of hosts, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your female servant, and remember me, and not forget your female servant, but give your female servant a male child, then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life[b], and no razor shall come upon his head.”

spob.text: She made this vow: “Yahweh of Heaven’s Armies, if you will truly see how I, your female servant, am suffering, remember me and do not forget me, and give me a male child, then I will give him to Yahweh for his whole life. No razor will ever touch his head.”[a]

pob.text: Then Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead. And all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash[a], “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”

pob.text: Then he took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces[a], and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, “Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.” Then the dread of Yahweh fell on the people[d][c][b], and they came out as one man.

pob.text: David came to the two hundred men who had become too exhausted to follow after David[a], and whom they had left at the Brook Besor. They came out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him[b], and David approached the people and asked them how they were.

pob.text: Then every wicked and worthless man from among the men who had gone with David answered and said[a], “Because they did not go with me, we will not give them any of the spoil that we recovered[c][b], except that each man may take his wife and his children and lead them away and go.”

pob.text: But David said[a], “You must not do so, my brothers, with what Yahweh has given us[c][b]. He has preserved us and has given into our hand the raiding band that came against us.”

pob.text: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as is the share of the one who goes down into the battle[a], so is the share of the one who stays by the supplies[b]; together they shall divide.

spob.text: Who would agree with you about this? The one who goes down into battle will receive the same share as the one who stays behind with the supplies. They will divide it together.

pob.text: Then all the valiant men arose and went all night[a], and they took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan[b], and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.

spob.text: Then all the brave fighting men set out and traveled through the night. They took Saul’s body and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. They went to Jabesh[a] and burned the bodies there.

public_domain_references.bsb: all their men of valor set out, journeyed all night, and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. When they arrived at Jabesh, they burned the bodies there.

public_domain_references.brenton: And they rose up, [even] every man of might, and marched all night, and took the body of Saul and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Bæthsam; and they bring them to Jabis, and burn them there.

pob.text: They took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh[b][a], and they fasted seven days.

spob.text: They took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh-gilead. Then they fasted, going without food for seven days.
